svg.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Ember classification order
svg.desc: Each transaction goes down the ladder until the first question answered yes. 1 a snippet in neutral becomes neutral. 2 a card purchase on a bill that has not opened yet becomes a future commitment. 3 a credit on the card becomes neutral or refund. 4 money into the account follows the income list: your rules, salary, Receita Federal (tax refund), loan, account owner, refund, interest income and cashback, and finally income to classify. 5 spending with a future date becomes a future commitment. 6 a bill payment or a transfer from the account owner becomes neutral. 7 your split creates two or more rows. 8 your pattern gives your category. 9 generic pattern. 10 CNAE of the CNPJ through BrasilAPI. 11 the card merchant category code, MCC. 12 a trusted Pluggy category. The rest falls into the gray zone; a counterparty under 300 reais a year becomes Miscellaneous (small).
svg.text: How a transaction gets a type and a category
goes down to the first yes; your rules come before the generic ones
A counterparty worth R$ 300 or more a year stays in the gray zone, so it can become a rule.
